payload.headline: Meta falls 5.93% to 560.84, breaks support; still wait for January earnings

summary.thesis: Meta's sales are still growing fast, but costs are rising faster, so cash flow has shrunk and the price still assumes a recovery that hasn't shown up yet.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait. Neither changes until the price reaches a better level or the 2027-01-27 report shows margins recovering.
summary.act_at: Buy at 475.85; no swing trade until a close back above 586.24

payload.happening: Meta fell 5.93% to 560.84. It closed below 576.61, the bottom of the support zone named in yesterday's note, and now sits just above the next support zone at 552.95–558.77. The stock is in a downtrend and trades below its 20-day (618.56), 50-day (676.6) and 200-day (627.89) averages. The Verge reported that a UN court cited military Facebook posts when it found Myanmar guilty of genocide. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand is not the problem. Revenue grew 27.53% over the last twelve months to 241.6B, though quarterly growth slowed to 26.07% from 33.08% two quarters ago. The problem is cost. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, fell to 32.86% from 43.23%. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending, dropped to 28.6B from 44.8B, and the free-cash-flow margin is only 11.86%. The balance sheet has shifted too: debt is 83.7B against 11.2B of cash, so net cash is -1.2B, though liquidity of 82.4B leaves room to keep operating. The filings flag that profit per share is lagging sales and that last quarter missed forecasts by 29%. All of this changes the business: what's at risk is how much cash each dollar of sales turns into. The Myanmar ruling and the reported insider sales of $14.1M outside pre-set plans are governance and sentiment matters (reputation and possible regulatory pressure, general knowledge). Today's data shows no direct effect from them on demand or margins. Gross margin of 81.03% shows the core product is still very profitable.

worth.text: At 560.84, Meta trades at 19.2 times trailing earnings and 6.0 times sales, the same as the peer median of 6.0. Adjusted for growth it is roughly in line with peers (1.01), and its price-to-sales sits at the 32nd percentile of its own five-year range, so it is cheap against its own past. The cash-flow model (DCF, a value based on future cash) disagrees. Starting from 28.6B of free cash flow, it gives 242.15 (bear), 370.49 (base) and 503.26 (bull), all below the price. The price implies starting cash-flow growth of 35.1%, while the growth inputs are 28%, 24% and 17%. Even 30% growth only gives 465.52. The gap between methods comes down to one thing: the DCF starts from today's shrunken cash flow, while the price-to-sales history assumes margins like the past. If operating margin fell to 24%, the model gives 238.97. My range runs from the low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history to its midpoint.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the heavy spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Revenue is still growing 27.53% a year to 241.6B, with a 3-year growth rate of about 23.9%, so demand is intact.
Gross margin of 81.03% shows the core ads business is very profitable, so the margin squeeze comes from spending, not weak pricing.
Price-to-sales of 6.0 equals the peer median and sits at only the 32nd percentile of Meta's own five-year range.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, and the DCF bull value of 503.26 is still below the 560.84 price.
Operating margin dropped to 32.86% from 43.23%, and last quarter missed forecasts by 29%.
Net cash is -1.2B with 83.7B of debt, and the trend is down, with the price below the 200-day average of 627.89.

levels.what: Bottom of the current support zone (552.95–558.77, 2 touches). A close below it opens the 535.39–541.21 zone and means the downtrend is continuing.
The DCF bull value. Below it, the price no longer sits above every cash-flow estimate.
Buy level: the low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 465.52 DCF value at 30% growth. Buying here does not depend on a full margin recovery.

longterm.why: At 560.84 the price is still above every DCF value, the business is graded C, and cash flow is falling. Buying now means paying in advance for a margin recovery the January report has not yet shown.

swing.why: The trend is down and the technical read is negative. The nearest resistance at 576.61 is less than one average daily move (ATR 23.27) away, which leaves too little room for a target. No trade unless the price closes back above 586.24, the top of the support zone it just broke.

decision.timing: Options price a 9.8% move by Dec 18 and a 17.7% move by Feb 19, which includes the 2027-01-27 report. That report is the deciding event, so there is no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin rising back toward 43.23% from 32.86%, or free cash flow growing again from 28.6B. That would support buying above 475.85.
Operating margin falls toward 24% instead. The DCF value at that margin is 238.97, which would move the stance from wait to avoid.
A close back above 586.24 on the daily chart would turn the swing view to enter, with a stop below 576.61.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The close at 560.84, below 576.61, confirmed the downtrend signal that yesterday's note flagged.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
